fine_trace.code: hb_blob_t *blob = hb_blob_create ((const char *)data, size, HB_MEMORY_MODE_READONLY, NULL, NULL);
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled font bytes are wrapped in a blob and used to create the face that will be subset.
The face is created from the attacker-controlled blob; its tables (cmap, glyf, loca, hmtx, etc.) are parsed from the input bytes.
A fresh hb_set_t is obtained from the subset input; its page_map vector is initialized with len=0 and arrayZ pointing at the 1-element static_array.
Codepoints are added to the set; each add calls page_for_insert which grows page_map via hb_set_t::resize, keeping page_map.len and pages.len in sync.
A second hb_set_t is created to hold glyph IDs; its page_map is also initialized with len=0.
Glyph 0 is added, so page_map.len becomes 1 and page_map[0] is initialized with major=0, index=0.
For each requested codepoint the cmap is consulted; a malformed cmap can return a gid that is out of range for the glyf/loca tables.
The gid from the cmap is added to the retain set; if the cmap yields a gid beyond the actual glyf/loca glyph count, that gid is still retained.
For each retained gid, get_composite is attempted; for an out-of-range gid get_offsets returns false and get_composite returns false, so no children are added.
The retained gids (including the out-of-range gid from the cmap) are pushed into plan->glyphs in sorted order.
For every glyph in plan->glyphs, two instruction-range slots are appended and zero-initialized, so instruction_ranges.len == 2 * glyph_ids.len.
For the out-of-range gid, get_offsets returns false because glyph >= num_glyphs; the loop continues with instruction_ranges entries left at 0.
The same out-of-range gid fails get_offsets again, so start_offset=end_offset=0 and length becomes 0; a zero-length glyph is written.

fine_trace.code: unsigned int instruction_start = instruction_ranges[i * 2]; unsigned int instruction_end = instruction_ranges[i * 2 + 1];
fine_trace.note: instruction_ranges entries are read; they were zero-initialized in the size pass, so no uninitialized read occurs here in this version.
length is 0 for the invalid glyph; the zero-length glyph is memcpy'd and the loca entry is written, keeping the output consistent.
A malformed cmap format 4 subtable can return a gid that is not present in the glyf/loca tables; this gid is retained and later processed by the glyf subsetter.
When get_offsets fails for a retained gid, the code sets start_offset=end_offset=0, so the glyph is treated as zero-length and no uninitialized offset is used.
For the invalid glyph length is 0; the subsequent memcpy with length 0 and the loca write are safe, so the glyf path does not read uninitialized memory.

fine_trace.code: glyf_prime_data_next += length + (length % 2); // Align to 2 bytes for short loca.
fine_trace.note: The write pointer advances by 0 for the invalid glyph; the output glyf/loca tables remain consistent with the size computed in the size pass.
The subset glyf and loca blobs are created from the fully initialized buffers; no uninitialized bytes are exposed in this path.
